answer: Each new identity tied to the same funding source pays a levy equal to 0.01 ocean times the square of that source's active identity count, so the tenth identity costs 1 ocean while the hundredth costs 100 ocean. A cartel can still add agents, but its per-identity cost climbs steeply, and an atlas mapping shared funding links makes evasion visible without blocking entry. The same curve applies to mesa-based agents and any other runtime, so cloning identities becomes a budget problem rather than a gate.
